rubric.why: Awards one mark for stating what magnification describes.
rubric.description: Magnification describes how much larger the image appears than the object.
rubric.how: Look for a statement connecting magnification with image size or enlargement of the object.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for stating what resolution describes.
rubric.description: Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that resolution determines whether close points can be seen separately.

modelAnswer: Magnification is how many times larger an image appears than the actual object.
Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a haploid and a diploid generation.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for identifying the two generations that alternate.
rubric.description: The life cycle alternates between gametophyte and sporophyte generations.
rubric.how: Look for both generation names and their alternation.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for stating their ploidy difference.
rubric.description: The gametophyte is haploid and the sporophyte is diploid.
rubric.how: Look for the correct haploid/diploid distinction.

modelAnswer: Alternation of generations is a life cycle in which the haploid gametophyte and diploid sporophyte generations alternate.
The gametophyte produces gametes, while the sporophyte produces spores.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for describing chromatin in the nucleus between divisions.
rubric.description: Chromatin is the diffuse, thread-like material present in the nucleus during interphase.
rubric.how: Look for its thread-like or diffuse form and association with interphase.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for describing chromosomes during cell division.
rubric.description: Chromosomes are condensed structures formed from chromatin and visible during cell division.
rubric.how: Look for condensation or visibility during cell division.

modelAnswer: Chromatin is the long, thin, thread-like form of genetic material in the nucleus during interphase.
Chromosomes are condensed forms of chromatin that become visible during cell division.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for identifying the cell component that divides.
rubric.description: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Look for an explicit reference to division of the cytoplasm.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for stating when it occurs or its result.
rubric.description: It follows nuclear division and separates the cell into two daughter cells.
rubric.how: Look for its sequence after nuclear division or the formation of daughter cells.

modelAnswer: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm after nuclear division.
It separates the cell into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Name two enzymes involved in digestion.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for naming a valid enzyme.
rubric.how: Accept a valid enzyme, for example amylase, lipase, pepsin or trypsin.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for naming a second valid enzyme.
rubric.how: The second enzyme must be different from the first.

modelAnswer: Amylase and lipase are two enzymes.

items.followUp: Define a catalyst and state its effect on activation energy.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for identifying activation energy as an energy requirement.
rubric.description: Activation energy is the minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Look for the minimum or least energy needed to initiate a reaction.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for stating its role in starting the reaction.
rubric.description: This energy enables the chemical reaction to begin.
rubric.how: Look for a connection between the energy and starting or initiating the reaction.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: In which year was ATP discovered, and who discovered it?

rubric.why: Awards one mark for the correct year.
rubric.description: Karl Lohmann made the discovery in 1929.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for identifying what was discovered.
rubric.how: Look for ATP or its full name.

modelAnswer: Karl Lohmann discovered ATP (adenosine triphosphate) in 1929.

items.followUp: Name two products of aerobic respiration besides carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for naming a respiratory product.
rubric.description: Carbon dioxide is produced during respiration.
rubric.how: Look for carbon dioxide or its formula, CO2.

rubric.why: Awards one mark for naming the other respiratory product.
rubric.how: Look for water or its formula, H2O.

modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide and water are produced during respiration.
